title: Intuitive Eating: A Revolutionary Program That Works
author: Evelyn Tribole
Elyse Resch
target_audience: Adults seeking a healthy relationship with food
Individuals recovering from chronic dieting or disordered eating
Anyone interested in weight-neutral wellness approaches
core_themes: Reconnecting with inner hunger and fullness cues
Healing from the effects of diet culture
primary_purpose: To provide a practical, evidence-based approach for rejecting restrictive diet culture and cultivating a peaceful, trusting relationship with food and body through the attunement to natural hunger, fullness, and satisfaction signals.

structure_format.organization: Divided into sections explaining the ten core principles of Intuitive Eating, with supporting stories, research, exercises, and FAQs
features: Step-by-step breakdown of each Intuitive Eating principle

key_concepts_lessons: Dieting is biologically and psychologically counterproductive, often leading to weight cycling and disordered eating.
Body attunement—learning to recognize physical hunger and fullness cues—restores trust between mind and body.
Food should be approached without moral judgment; all foods fit without guilt.
Emotional eating is addressed with compassion and by developing alternative coping mechanisms.
Respect and care for the body at any size promotes overall well-being.
Physical activity is reframed as self-care, not punishment.
notable_features: Ten clearly defined principles forming a practical roadmap
Inclusion of first-person stories and real-world examples
Revised editions reflect up-to-date research and social awareness (e.g., Health at Every Size, body diversity)
cultural_historical_context: Originally published in the mid-1990s as backlash to the prevailing diet-centric and thin-ideal wellness culture, Intuitive Eating has gained renewed attention with the rise of anti-diet movements, body positivity, and holistic well-being trends. The fourth edition incorporates decades of expanded research and cultural shifts regarding weight bias and health.
reception_impact: Widely regarded as foundational in the anti-diet and Health at Every Size (HAES) spaces
Praised for shifting the conversation from weight to well-being
Adopted by therapists, dietitians, and researchers globally
Critics sometimes challenge its departure from traditional weight-loss paradigms and the application in certain medical contexts
comparable_titles: The Eating Instinct: Food Culture, Body Image, and Guilt in America by Virginia Sole-Smith
Health at Every Size by Linda Bacon
Body Respect by Linda Bacon and Lucy Aphramor
